params.body:
Phase 2 of the sources plan (`docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`): the academic indexes.

## What the week shows
From `adapter_runs`, 23 to 30 September:
- Semantic Scholar delivered **0 new papers**: every round that asked was refused with a rate limit.
- OpenAlex delivered 8, and was refused (HTTP 429) 10 times.

One request from the box on 2026-09-30 says why, in both APIs' own words:
- OpenAlex: "Anonymous search is temporarily rate-limited while the search cluster is under elevated load. Please retry in 38s, or use a free API key for uninterrupted access". The `mailto` no longer buys the polite pool.
- Semantic Scholar: "Too Many Requests. Please wait and try again or apply for a key for higher rate limits". The keyless bulk endpoint the adapter was built on is closed too.

## What this changes
- **OpenAlex reads `OPENALEX_API_KEY`** and sends it as `api_key` when set. Semantic Scholar already read `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY`. Both stay optional in the adapter declaration test.
- **A refusal ends the round.** Both adapters stop at the first rate limit instead of asking the other fourteen queries. The queries not asked keep no mark and stay due for the next round.
- **OpenAlex's 429 is named "rate limit"**, so collect counts it as ours (the `OURS` rule) and never parks a healthy query for it. Until now it read "OpenAlex HTTP 429", which the rule did not match. No query was parked yet, because the same rows also get successful runs.
- **Both keys are declared to Elixir** in `/api/elixir` when set, like the Together key: proven by the adapter's last delivery, refused by a rate limit after it, never the value. Tested.
- Two comments that described the old situation (the polite pool; the open bulk endpoint) say what is true now.

## What it needs
Two free keys, requested by a person:
- OpenAlex, via https://openalex.org/rest-api
- Semantic Scholar, via https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api#api-key-form

Each goes into the pipeline's environment settings on the box, under the two names above. Without them nothing breaks: OpenAlex keeps getting through part of the time, and Semantic Scholar stays silent, which the Collection screen shows.

Tests: 959 pass. Lint: 0 undefined names, unused unchanged.
params.title: The academic indexes take a key, stop at the first refusal, and never park a query for it
